title: Introduce mini-span proxy and deferred-span emission for inference hotpath
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The inference hotpath emits full trace spans synchronously for every request, which creates allocation pressure and increases tail latency at high QPS. Our current prefilter samplers reduce volume but still require short-lived allocations and some string/metadata formatting on the hotpath. Goal: Reduce CPU and allocation overhead on the critical inference path by replacing full immediate span assembly with a lightweight in-process 'mini-span' proxy that records a compact fingerprint and tiny metadata, and defers full span assembly and encoding to an async worker (deferred-span emitter). This ticket covers design, runtime changes, compatibility hooks for tracing integrations, and a staged rollout with feature flags and telemetry to validate correctness and perf gains.
background:
- Observability team baseline traces show >12% CPU at p99 under peak QPS attributable to span formatting and encode allocations.
- We already have prefilter and probabilistic samplers, but they leave the hotpath responsible for allocating span objects and headers.
- Inference runtime has strict SLOs; improvements must keep semantic fidelity for sampled traces and not break existing tracing consumers (Jaeger/Zipkin/OpenTelemetry export paths).
approach:
- Introduce a tiny MiniSpan struct on hotpath (fixed-size, no heap strings): {trace_id, span_id, parent_id, start_ts, duration_hint, fingerprint_code, route_id, sample_hint}.
- Replace hotpath full-span build with mini-span capture and write to a bounded lock-free ring buffer per worker.
- Implement a DeferredSpanEmitter background pool that pops mini-spans, reconstructs the full span by joining contextual metadata (request headers, route mapping) and performs final encoding/submit to exporter asynchronously.
- Add safety fallback: if ring buffer is full, increment a metric and fall back to a very-low-cost counter-only telemetry event (drop + tally) to avoid blocking hotpath.
- Expose a per-tenant budget controller that limits deferred emission rate and applies probabilistic promotion of mini-spans to full spans based on tenant SLAs.
- Provide tracing hooks and compatibility shim so downstream exporters see the same span IDs/timestamps when a mini-span is promoted to a full span.
- Feature flag + rollout plan: start internal Canary, then opt-in customers, then global release with automatic rollback if p99 latency regresses >5% or CPU exceeds threshold.
design_decisions: Use fixed-size mini-span to avoid heap allocations on hotpath
Bounded ring buffers per worker to minimize contention
Deferred emitter runs with CPU QoS class and soft-rate limiting to avoid impacting inference workers
Keep exact span ids so sampled traces can be correlated end-to-end even when deferred
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Lost context (headers/env) needed to reconstruct span -> Mitigation: buffer minimal header hash and lookup contextual store; fallback to 'partial' span if unavailable
Risk: Ring buffer saturation under traffic spikes -> Mitigation: backpressure metrics, drop counter and circuit-breaker promotion to counter-only telemetry
Risk: Tracing consumers assume immediate spans for latency correlations -> Mitigation: compatibility shim with identical timestamps and explicit meta field indicating deferred emission
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath p99 CPU < baseline -8% at target QPS during internal canary
End-to-end sampled traces preserve trace/span IDs and have consistent timestamps for promoted spans
Deferred emitter does not increase observed trace consumer error rate by >1%
Ring buffer full events < 0.1% of requests at steady state in canary
Feature flag allows safe rollback without data loss
implementation_notes: Prototype in the C++ inference runtime first (lowest overhead), with a Go shim for the deferred emitter used by control-plane services
Create OTel-compatible exporter plugin to allow downstream systems to consume deferred spans without modification
Add a small Confluence design doc and sequence diagram before engineering spike: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/MiniSpan+Deferred+Emitter
